info.title: Fix import failing on single invalid row

metadata.displayText:
There is an issue with our import flow which results in an import failing if a single row is invalid. This is not ideal and we need to resolve it. 

I have review the code in the ImportController, ProcessImportJob and ImportJob. And i think we can fix and improve it with the following: 

- Validating the filetype/size/header and store it using a unique internal filename,
- Hash the file and check for matching pending or processing imports before createing another job, 
- Process the CSV row-by-row rather than loading it entirely into memory. Invalid rows are recorded and skipped rather than aborting the transaction.
- Track total, processed, successful and failed row counts, updating them periodically while the worker runs.
- Store row number, original row data and validation errors in an import_job_errors table.
- Generate a CSV containing rejected records and their error reasons, expose it through a download endpoint, and automatically delete it after a defined TTL.

I have added a test under `ProcessImportJobTest` which currently will fail and checks to make sure a single row can not cause the import to fail. You will need to extend on this for the functionality being added above. Before you start make a Plan.md which outlines the changes to be made

# Plan — Resilient CSV Import (Scenario 3)

## 1. Problem statement

`app/Jobs/ProcessImportJob.php:44-54` wraps all rows in a single `DB::transaction()`
with no per-row validation. One invalid row (bad email, duplicate email, missing
name) throws and rolls back the entire import, `failed()` marks the job `failed`,
and valid rows are lost.

Secondary issues:

- `app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:18-20` stores upload under the
  client-provided filename (`storeAs('imports', $filename)`). Collisions/overwrites
  and path-traversal-prone; no header check; no dedupe.
- `app/Models/ImportJob.php:22-28` / `database/migrations/2024_01_01_300000_create_import_jobs_table.php:11-18`
  only track `total_rows`, `processed_rows`. No `successful_rows` / `failed_rows`,
  no row-level error store, statuses limited to `pending|processing|completed|failed`.
- `app/Jobs/ProcessImportJob.php:32-40` loads the whole CSV into `$rows` array —
  unbounded memory on large files.
- No rejected-rows artifact for operators to fix/retry.

Failing acceptance test: `tests/Feature/ProcessImportJobTest.php:15-56`
expects `completed_with_errors` + `total/processed/successful/failed` counts.
It fails today (missing columns + abort-on-error behaviour).

## 2. Changes to be made

### 2.1 `ImportController@store` — validation + safe storage + dedupe
File: `app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:12-33`

- Keep `required|file|mimes:csv,txt|max:10240`, add explicit `min:1` / empty-file
  guard and a header check: first line must contain exactly
  `name,email,password` (trimmed, case-sensitive). Return `422` with
  `header` error key if mismatch — fail fast before a job row is created.
- Store with unique internal name, never client name:
  `storeAs('imports', Str::uuid().'.csv')`. Persist both:
  `original_filename` (display) + `stored_path` (internal, e.g. `imports/<uuid>.csv`).
  Keep legacy `filename` column populated for BC, or rename/migrate (see §3).
- Hash file for dedupe: `hash_file('sha256', $storedFullPath)` → `file_hash`.

bad-format rows are now rejected instead of inserted, one proving a
constraint-violating row no longer rolls back its siblings.

  same job never duplicates `import_job_errors` rows. Document that enabling
  `$tries > 1` later requires offset-resume (skip `processed_rows`) — out of
  scope here.
- Stream: `fopen` + `fgetcsv` loop (or `LazyCollection`), never accumulate `$rows`.
  Use `SplFileObject`/`fgetcsv` with `array_combine` guarded for column-count
  mismatch (short/long rows → record error, continue).
- Per row (inside loop, no outer transaction):
  1. `Validator::make($row, ['name'=>'required|string|max:255','email'=>'required|email|unique:users,email','password'=>'nullable|string|min:8'])`.

     `password123` when implementation lands (or consciously relax the rule to
     `min:6`); the upload-only test passes either way today because it fakes
     the bus, but the inconsistency must not be left latent.
  2. On failure → `import_job_errors` upsert + `$failed++`.

## 5. Out of scope / tradeoffs

- No chunked/batch insert — per-row inserts are slower but required for row
  isolation; revisit with batch+savepoints only if throughput demands it.
- Email `unique` validator has inherent TOCTOU race; the index-specific
  duplicate catch (§2.3) is the backstop — anything not provably a
  `users.email` unique violation still fails the job.
- Plaintext passwords are never written to `import_job_errors` or the rejected
  CSV; only the salted hash reaches `users`. Operators lose the ability to see
  the exact rejected password value — accepted, since the reason string is
  sufficient to fix and re-upload.
- Stale threshold (default 30 min) trades false-reaps of very slow healthy
  imports (mitigated by the flush heartbeat) against indefinite dedupe blocks.
- Very large files: single worker, single pass; horizontal sharding explicitly
  out of scope. Periodic counter flushes are progress signals only; crash
  durability comes from the exception-path flush (§2.3), and hard kills can
  still lose at most one flush interval.
- Retries disabled (`$tries = 1`); resume-from-offset is a future extension.
- TTL default 7 days; download is unauthenticated like existing endpoints.

1: # Plan — Resilient CSV Import (Scenario 3)

3: ## 1. Problem statement (corrected)
4: 
5: `app/Jobs/ProcessImportJob.php:44-54` wraps all rows in a single `DB::transaction()`
6: with **no per-row validation**. Two distinct cases must not be conflated:
7: 
8: - **Case A — malformed-but-insertable row (e.g. `not-an-email`): does NOT throw
9:   today.** There is no `Validator` in the job, and
10:   `database/migrations/0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table.php:18` declares
11:   `email` as a plain `string()->unique()` — no format constraint. `User::create()`
12:   therefore inserts `not-an-email` successfully and the batch *commits*. The bug
13:   here is silent bad data, not a rollback. The provided acceptance test
14:   (`tests/Feature/ProcessImportJobTest.php:15-56`) exposes this: it expects the
15:   bad-format row to be *rejected* (`failed_rows=1`, absent from `users`), which
16:   the current code cannot do.
17: - **Case B — duplicate email: DOES abort the whole batch.** The second insert
18:   violates the unique index → `QueryException` (SQLSTATE 23000) → the outer
19:   transaction rolls back *all* rows, `failed()` marks the job `failed`, valid
20:   rows are lost. Same outcome for any DB-level throw inside the loop
21:   (e.g. `array_combine()` `ValueError` on column-count mismatch in PHP 8,
22:   thrown *before* the transaction at `ProcessImportJob.php:37`).
23: 
24: So the plan needs different tests for the two cases (see §4): one proving
25: bad-format rows are now rejected instead of inserted, one proving a
26: constraint-violating row no longer rolls back its siblings.
27: 
28: Secondary issues:
29: 
30: - `app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:18-20` stores upload under the
31:   client-provided filename (`storeAs('imports', $filename)`). Collisions/overwrites
32:   and path-traversal-prone; no header check; no dedupe.
33: - `app/Models/ImportJob.php:22-28` / `database/migrations/2024_01_01_300000_create_import_jobs_table.php:11-18`
34:   only track `total_rows`, `processed_rows`. No `successful_rows` / `failed_rows`,
35:   no row-level error store, statuses limited to `pending|processing|completed|failed`.
36: - `app/Jobs/ProcessImportJob.php:32-40` loads the whole CSV into `$rows` array —
37:   unbounded memory on large files.
38: - No rejected-rows artifact for operators to fix/retry.
39: 
40: Failing acceptance test: `tests/Feature/ProcessImportJobTest.php:15-56`
41: expects `completed_with_errors` + `total/processed/successful/failed` counts.
42: It fails today (missing columns + abort-on-error behaviour).
43: 
44: ## 2. Changes to be made
45: 
46: ### 2.1 `ImportController@store` — validation + safe storage + dedupe
47: File: `app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:12-33`
48: 
49: - Keep `required|file|mimes:csv,txt|max:10240`, add explicit empty-file guard
50:   and a header check. Normalise the header before comparing: strip a leading
51:   UTF-8 BOM (`\xEF\xBB\xBF`, as emitted by Excel/Sheets exports) from the first
52:   cell, trim whitespace/`\r` per cell, then require exactly
53:   `name,email,password` (case-sensitive after normalisation). Return `422` with
54:   a `header` error key on mismatch — fail fast before a job row is created.
55:   Shared `normaliseHeader()` helper used by both controller and worker so a
56:   BOM-prefixed file is not rejected in one place and accepted in the other.
57: - Store with unique internal name, never client name:
58:   `storeAs('imports', Str::uuid().'.csv')`. Persist both:
59:   `original_filename` (display) + `stored_path` (internal, e.g. `imports/<uuid>.csv`).
60:   Keep legacy `filename` column populated for BC, or rename/migrate (see §3).
61:   Ordering / orphan rule: hash and header-check the **temporary upload**
62:   (`$file->getRealPath()`) *before* storing. Only a file that passes the header
63:   check and the dedupe pre-check is stored. If the request ends in `422` or
64:   `409`, nothing is left on disk. Residual race case (pre-check passed, but the
65:   `UNIQUE(dedupe_key)` insert then collides): delete the just-stored copy
66:   before returning `409`, so duplicate uploads never accumulate unreferenced
67:   files. Tests assert the 409 path leaves no orphan in `imports/`.
68: - Hash file for dedupe: `hash_file('sha256', $file->getRealPath())` on the temp
69:   upload → `file_hash`. Before storing, query for an existing row with the same
70:   `file_hash` and `status IN ('pending','processing')` **that is not stale**
71:   (see stale rule below). If found, return `409` with `{ existing_job_id }`
72:   without storing anything.
73: - Race safety (revised): a lookup-then-insert inside a transaction is **not**
74:   race-safe — two concurrent uploads can both read "no active job" and both
75:   insert. And a plain `UNIQUE(file_hash)` is wrong: it would permanently forbid
76:   re-importing a file after the first import *completes*. DB-enforced rule:
77:   add `dedupe_key CHAR(64) NULL UNIQUE` alongside the non-unique `file_hash`
78:   history column, plus `processing_started_at TIMESTAMP NULL` as the lock
79:   heartbeat. Set `dedupe_key = file_hash` on create; clear it to `NULL` in
80:   the same write that moves the job to a terminal state (`completed`,
81:   `completed_with_errors`, `failed`). Both MySQL and SQLite permit multiple
82:   `NULL`s in a unique index, so only one *active* job per hash can exist while
83:   completed jobs remain re-importable. Create path catches the duplicate-key
84:   `QueryException` (SQLSTATE 23000) and, on collision, re-queries the live row
85:   and returns `409` (deleting any just-stored copy first) — the catch, not the
86:   pre-check, is the correctness mechanism. (A Redis/cache lock was considered
87:   and rejected: adds infra, not transactional with the row insert.)
88: - Stale-lock recovery: if a worker dies (SIGKILL, OOM, deploy) between the
89:   `processing` write and any terminal write, `failed()` never runs and
90:   `dedupe_key` stays occupied, blocking that file forever. Fix with an expiring
91:   lock: `processing_started_at` is set when the job enters `processing`
92:   (refreshed on each periodic counter flush as a heartbeat). A job is **stale**
93:   when `status = 'processing'` and `processing_started_at < now() - threshold`
94:   (`config('imports.stale_after_minutes', 30)`). Controller ignores stale rows
95:   in the pre-check; on a duplicate-key collision against a stale row it reaps
96:   it (marks `failed` with `error_message = 'Stale worker; lock reclaimed.'`,
97:   nulls `dedupe_key`) and retries the insert once. A scheduled
98:   `imports:reap-stale` command (folded into the prune command or standalone,
99:   run every 10 min) reaps stale jobs with no new upload in flight. Worker
100:   heartbeat via the periodic flush keeps long-but-healthy imports from looking
101:   stale.
102: - Return `202 { id, status }` unchanged on success.
103: 
104: ### 2.2 Migration: extend `import_jobs`, add `import_job_errors`
105: New migration(s), e.g. `2026_09_30_000001_extend_import_jobs_table.php`:
106: 
107: `import_jobs` additions:
108: 
109: - `original_filename string nullable`
110: - `stored_path string nullable` (internal disk path)
111: - `file_hash char(64) nullable, index` (history / audit; NOT unique)
112: - `dedupe_key char(64) nullable, unique` (active-job lock; set on create,
113:   nulled on terminal state — see §2.1)
114: - `processing_started_at timestamp nullable` (lock heartbeat / stale detection;
115:   set on entering `processing`, refreshed on each counter flush)
116: - `successful_rows integer default 0`
117: - `failed_rows integer default 0`
118: - `rejected_path string nullable` (path to generated rejects CSV)
119: - `rejected_expires_at timestamp nullable` (TTL marker)
120: - extend `status` comment/enum to include `completed_with_errors`
121:   (keep string column, validate in code, not DB enum for portability).
122: 
123: New table `import_job_errors`:
124: 
125: - `id`, `import_job_id FK -> import_jobs.id cascadeOnDelete, index`
126: - `row_number unsignedInteger` (1-based data-row number, header = row 1 excluded)
127: - `row_data json` — **redacted**: stores only non-sensitive fields
128:   (`{ "name": ..., "email": ... }`). The CSV `password` value is **never**
129:   persisted here (or anywhere except the salted `users.password` hash). A
130:   password validation failure is recorded as a reason
131:   (e.g. `{"password": ["The password must be at least 8 characters."]}`)
132:   without retaining its value. If raw-row forensics are ever needed, store
133:   `password_present: bool` only.
134: - `errors json` (`['email'=>[...], ...]` from validator)
135: - `timestamps`
136: - `unique(['import_job_id','row_number'])` — makes error writes idempotent
137:   across at-least-once redelivery (worker uses `updateOrCreate`, see §2.3).
138: 
139: Update `app/Models/ImportJob.php:20-29`: `$fillable` + casts + `errors()` HasMany
140: relation; new `app/Models/ImportJobError.php` model.
141: 
142: ### 2.3 `ProcessImportJob` — row-by-row streaming, per-row validation
143: File: `app/Jobs/ProcessImportJob.php:18-60` (rewrite `handle()`):
144: 
145: - Resolve path via `stored_path` (fall back to legacy `imports/{filename}`).
146:   Missing file → `failed` + `error_message`, as today.
147: - Validate header again in worker (defence in depth) with the same
148:   BOM-stripping `normaliseHeader()`; mismatch → `failed`.
149: - Retry / double-processing rule (resolved): rows commit individually (no outer
150:   transaction), so a queue retry that restarts from row 1 would re-insert
151:   already-created users and mislabel them as row failures on the second pass.
152:   Decision: set `public $tries = 1` on the job (no automatic retry). There is
153:   **no supported same-job rerun path**: `handle()` starts with `refresh()` and
154:   exits as a no-op if the job is already terminal (`completed`,
155:   `completed_with_errors`, `failed`), so re-dispatching a completed job never
156:   modifies users, counters, or error rows. To reprocess, upload again (new
157:   `ImportJob`; allowed because the terminal write nulled `dedupe_key`). The
158:   `updateOrCreate(['import_job_id','row_number'])` + unique constraint on error
159:   rows is **not** a rerun feature — it only guards the at-least-once redelivery
160:   edge (duplicate dispatch / `queue:retry` of a still-`processing` job after a
161:   crash) against double-inserting error rows. Enabling `$tries > 1` later
162:   requires offset-resume (skip `processed_rows`) — out of scope here.
163: - Stream: `fopen` + `fgetcsv` loop (or `LazyCollection`), never accumulate `$rows`.
164:   Use `SplFileObject`/`fgetcsv` with `array_combine` guarded for column-count
165:   mismatch (short/long rows → record error, continue).
166: - Per row (inside loop, no outer transaction):
167:   1. Normalise first, then validate the **defaulted** value: trim `name`/`email`;
168:      if `password` is missing/`null`/blank (`''` or whitespace-only), replace it
169:      with the default `'password'` **before** `Validator::make()`. Validate
170:      `['name'=>'required|string|max:255','email'=>'required|email|unique:users,email','password'=>'required|string|min:8']`
171:      (password `required` post-defaulting, not `nullable` — otherwise `''`
172:      fails `min:8` and contradicts the stated default). This makes "blank
173:      password → default → passes" deterministic rather than dependent on how
174:      `Validator` treats empty strings vs `null`.
175:      NOTE — fixture impact: `tests/Feature/ImportTest.php:23` uploads
176:      `...john@example.com,secret` (`secret` = 6 chars). Under `min:8` that row
177:      would now be *rejected* if ever processed. Update that fixture to
178:      `password123` when implementation lands (or consciously relax the rule to
179:      `min:6`); the upload-only test passes either way today because it fakes
180:      the bus, but the inconsistency must not be left latent.
181:   2. On failure → upsert redacted `import_job_errors` row
182:      (`row_data = {name, email}` only — never the password value) + `$failed++`.
183:   3. On pass → `try { User::create(['name','email','password' => Hash::make($row['password'])]) }`
184:      with **narrow** catch: only a proven unique-violation on `users.email` is
185:      a row error. Helper `isEmailDuplicate()` requires ALL of: SQLSTATE
186:      `23000`, plus driver-specific proof — MySQL `errorInfo[1] === 1062` with
187:      the message naming the email unique index (`users_email_unique`), or
188:      SQLite `errorInfo[1] === 19` with message matching
189:      `UNIQUE constraint failed: users.email`. Bare `23000` / bare code `19`
190:      also cover NOT-NULL, CHECK, and other indexes, so they alone are
191:      insufficient — any non-matching `QueryException` (connection loss, missing
192:      table, other constraint) is rethrown so an outage/schema error is never
193:      mislabelled as "1 bad CSV row". Duplicate-email → redacted error row +
194:      `$failed++`, else `$success++`.
195:   4. `$processed++`; every N rows (e.g. `50`/`100`) flush
196:      `processed/successful/failed/total` for live `GET /imports/{id}` progress.
197: - Counter durability (revised): periodic flush alone is lossy — `failed()` runs
198:   on a fresh model state and would otherwise preserve only the last flush,
199:   discarding rows handled since. So the loop body is wrapped in try/catch: the
200:   catch path flushes the in-memory `$processed/$success/$failed` counters to
201:   the DB *before* marking `failed` + `error_message`. `failed()` itself stays
202:   purely as a safety net (fatal/timeout where the catch never ran): it
203:   `refresh()`es, preserves existing counters, and only sets status/message —
204:   it never invents counts.
205: - Terminal status: `failed_rows === 0 ? 'completed' : 'completed_with_errors'`.
206:   The terminal write also nulls `dedupe_key` (releasing the §2.1 lock) in the
207:   same update.
208: - `total_rows`: increment as streamed, flushed with the periodic update, final
209:   sync at end. (Two-pass doubles I/O; document tradeoff.)
210: 
211: ### 2.4 Progress + error visibility in API
212: File: `app/Http/Controllers/ImportController.php:35-48`, `routes/api.php:18-19`
213: 
214: - `GET /api/imports/{id}` gains `successful_rows`, `failed_rows`,
215:   `original_filename`, `errors_count`, `rejected_url`/`rejected_expires_at`.
216:   Keep existing keys for BC.
217: - New `GET /api/imports/{id}/errors` (or `/rejected`): streams the rejects CSV as
218:   `text/csv` download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`). `404` if no failures or
219:   artifact expired/deleted. Authorisation: none today — keep same posture, note as
220:   follow-up.
221: 
222: ### 2.5 Rejected-rows CSV + TTL cleanup
223: 
224: - After processing, if `$failed > 0`, generate
225:   `imports/rejected/{import_job_id}.csv` with columns
226:   `row_number,name,email,errors` — **no password column** (`errors` = flattened
227:   `field: msg; …`; for password failures the reason is recorded without the
228:   value). The DB `import_job_errors.row_data` is likewise redacted (§2.2), so
229:   plaintext credentials exist nowhere outside the salted `users.password` hash.
230:   Store path in `import_jobs.rejected_path`, set
231:   `rejected_expires_at = now()+TTL`
232:   (TTL e.g. `7 days`, via `config('imports.rejected_ttl_days', 7)` or constant).
233: - Cleanup: `app/Console/Commands/PruneRejectedImportFiles.php`
234:   (`imports:prune-rejected`, also reaps stale `processing` jobs past
235:   `stale_after_minutes` — or a separate `imports:reap-stale` on a 10-min
236:   schedule) deletes expired files + nulls `rejected_path`,
237:   scheduled daily in `routes/console.php` (stale-reaper more frequently). Alternative: delayed queued job
238:   `DeleteRejectedFile::dispatch($job)->delay($ttl)` — prefer Artisan command for
239:   simplicity/idempotency; document choice.
240: - `Storage::disk('local')` throughout so `Storage::fake('local')` tests work.
241: 
242: ### 2.6 Config / docs
243: 
244: - Small `config/imports.php`: `chunk_flush` (progress update interval),
245:   `rejected_ttl_days`, `expected_headers`, `stale_after_minutes`. Avoid
246:   enterprise abstraction; plain constants acceptable if config file deemed
247:   overkill.
248: 
249: ## 3. Migration / BC notes
250: 
251: - Backfill: existing rows get `successful_rows=processed_rows`,
252:   `failed_rows=0`, `original_filename=filename`, `stored_path='imports/'.filename`,
253:   `file_hash=NULL`, `dedupe_key=NULL`, `processing_started_at=NULL`
254:   (no fake lock on history).
255: - Old `ImportTest.php:32` asserts `filename = users.csv` — keep writing client name
256:   into `filename` (or update test to assert `original_filename`). Decision at
257:   implementation: keep `filename` = original display name, `stored_path` = internal.
258: - Dedupe enforcement is the `UNIQUE(dedupe_key)` index + duplicate-key catch in
259:   the controller (see §2.1), not the pre-check transaction.
260: - `ImportTest.php:23` fixture uses password `secret` (6 chars): update to
261:   `password123` to satisfy the new `min:8` row rule.
262: 
263: ## 4. Test plan (extend `ProcessImportJobTest`, `ImportTest`)
264: 
265: Keep the provided `test_invalid_row_does_not_abort_import` as the acceptance test.
266: 
267: Additions in `tests/Feature/ProcessImportJobTest.php` (split by failure mode —
268: see §1):
269: 
270: - bad-format row (`not-an-email`) → `completed_with_errors`, `2/1` split,
271:   absent from `users`, error row present. (Regression: today this row is
272:   silently *inserted*.)
273: - duplicate-email row (second occurrence, or pre-seeded user) → isolated via
274:   `unique` validator / duplicate-key catch; siblings commit; no batch rollback.
275:   (Regression: today this rolls back everything.)
276: - all-valid import → `completed`, counts `3/3/3/0`, zero `import_job_errors`.
277: - all-invalid import → `completed_with_errors`, zero users created.
278: - malformed row (wrong column count) → skipped, recorded with `row_number` +
279:   `row_data` + `errors`.
280: - `import_job_errors` assertions: `row_number`, redacted `row_data` JSON
281:   (`name`/`email` only — assert password value absent), `errors` JSON keys;
282:   redelivery of a still-`processing` job does not duplicate error rows
283:   (`unique(import_job_id,row_number)`); re-dispatch after terminal status is a
284:   no-op (counters/users unchanged).
285: - blank-password row → succeeds via default `'password'` (assert user created,
286:   no error row); short-password row (e.g. `secret`) → rejected with reason,
287:   value not stored.
288: - BOM-prefixed header (`\xEF\xBB\xBFname,email,password`) imports normally.
289: - progress columns persisted (`successful_rows`/`failed_rows`).
290: 
291: Additions in `tests/Feature/ImportTest.php`:
292: 
293: - header rejection (`422` on bad header, no job created) + BOM-prefixed header
294:   accepted.
295: - unique internal storage (assert `stored_path !== original name`, file exists).
296: - duplicate upload while `pending/processing` → `409` + same `existing_job_id`,
297:   no second `ProcessImportJob` dispatched, no orphan file stored; re-upload after
298:   completion → `202` (new job allowed — `dedupe_key` was nulled); upload matching
299:   a stale `processing` job (backdated `processing_started_at`) → old job reaped
300:   as `failed`, new upload accepted.
301: - `GET /imports/{id}` exposes new counters.
302: - rejects download: `GET /api/imports/{id}/errors` returns CSV with bad row +
303:   reason and **no password column/values**; `404` when no failures; pruning
304:   command deletes expired file.
305: - error-record redaction: assert stored `row_data` and rejected CSV contain no
306:   password values even when the rejected row failed on password.
307: 
308: Run: `php artisan test --filter=Import` (SQLite in-memory per `phpunit.xml`).
309: 
310: ## 5. Out of scope / tradeoffs
311: 
312: - No chunked/batch insert — per-row inserts are slower but required for row
313:   isolation; revisit with batch+savepoints only if throughput demands it.
314: - Email `unique` validator has inherent TOCTOU race; the index-specific
315:   duplicate catch (§2.3) is the backstop — anything not provably a
316:   `users.email` unique violation still fails the job.
317: - Plaintext passwords are never written to `import_job_errors` or the rejected
318:   CSV; only the salted hash reaches `users`. Operators lose the ability to see
319:   the exact rejected password value — accepted, since the reason string is
320:   sufficient to fix and re-upload.
321: - Stale threshold (default 30 min) trades false-reaps of very slow healthy
322:   imports (mitigated by the flush heartbeat) against indefinite dedupe blocks.
323: - Very large files: single worker, single pass; horizontal sharding explicitly
324:   out of scope. Periodic counter flushes are progress signals only; crash
325:   durability comes from the exception-path flush (§2.3), and hard kills can
326:   still lose at most one flush interval.
327: - Retries disabled (`$tries = 1`); resume-from-offset is a future extension.
328: - TTL default 7 days; download is unauthenticated like existing endpoints.
329: 
330: ## 6. Implementation order
331: 
332: 1. Migration + models (`import_jobs` columns, `import_job_errors`).
333: 2. Controller: header check, UUID storage, hash + `409` dedupe.
334: 3. Job: streaming loop, per-row validator, counters, rejects CSV.
335: 4. `show` + `errors` download endpoint + prune command + schedule.
336: 5. Tests above; run full suite.

{
    /**
     * Normalise a parsed CSV header row: strip a leading UTF-8 BOM from the
     * first cell (Excel/Sheets exports), trim whitespace/CR per cell.
     *
     * @param  array<int, mixed>  $header
     * @return array<int, string>
     */
    public static function normaliseHeader(array $header): array
    {
        $cells = array_map(fn ($c) => trim((string) $c), $header);

        if (isset($cells[0])) {
            $cells[0] = ltrim($cells[0], "\xEF\xBB\xBF");
        }

        return array_values($cells);

    {
        if ($job->status !== 'processing' || $job->processing_started_at === null) {
            return false;
        }

        return $job->processing_started_at->lt(
            now()->subMinutes(self::staleThresholdMinutes())

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Jobs\ProcessImportJob;
use App\Models\ImportJob;
use App\Support\CsvImport;
use Illuminate\Database\QueryException;
use Illuminate\Http\JsonResponse;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\StreamedResponse;

class ImportController extends Controller
{
    public function store(Request $request): JsonResponse
    {
        $request->validate([
            'file' => 'required|file|mimes:csv,txt|max:10240',
        ]);

        $file = $request->file('file');
        $realPath = $file->getRealPath();

        if ($realPath === false || filesize($realPath) === 0) {
            return response()->json([
                'message' => 'The file is empty.',
                'errors' => ['file' => ['The file is empty.']],
            ], 422);
        }

        // Header check on the temp upload, before anything is stored.
        $handle = fopen($realPath, 'r');
        $header = $handle !== false ? fgetcsv($handle) : false;
        if ($handle !== false) {
            fclose($handle);
        }

        if ($header === false || ! CsvImport::headerValid($header)) {
            return response()->json([
                'message' => 'Invalid CSV header. Expected: name,email,password.',
                'errors' => ['header' => ['Invalid CSV header. Expected: name,email,password.']],
            ], 422);
        }

        $hash = hash_file('sha256', $realPath);

        // Fast-path pre-check (non-stale active job). The UNIQUE(dedupe_key)
        // catch below is the correctness mechanism under concurrency.
        $existing = ImportJob::where('file_hash', $hash)
            ->whereIn('status', ['pending', 'processing'])
            ->orderByDesc('id')
            ->get()
            ->first(fn (ImportJob $job) => ! CsvImport::isStale($job));

        if ($existing) {
            return response()->json([
                'message' => 'An import for this file is already pending or processing.',
                'existing_job_id' => $existing->id,
            ], 409);
        }

        $originalFilename = $file->getClientOriginalName();
        $storedPath = 'imports/' . (string) Str::uuid() . '.csv';
        $file->storeAs('imports', basename($storedPath));

        try {
            $job = ImportJob::create([
                'filename' => $originalFilename,
                'original_filename' => $originalFilename,
                'stored_path' => $storedPath,
                'file_hash' => $hash,
                'dedupe_key' => $hash,
                'status' => 'pending',
            ]);
        } catch (QueryException $e) {
            // Lost the race: another request inserted the same dedupe_key first.
            \Storage::disk('local')->delete($storedPath);

            $conflict = ImportJob::where('dedupe_key', $hash)->first();

            if ($conflict && CsvImport::isStale($conflict)) {
                $conflict->update([
                    'status' => 'failed',
                    'error_message' => 'Stale worker; lock reclaimed.',
                    'dedupe_key' => null,
                ]);

                $job = ImportJob::create([
                    'filename' => $originalFilename,
                    'original_filename' => $originalFilename,
                    'stored_path' => $storedPath,
                    'file_hash' => $hash,
                    'dedupe_key' => $hash,
                    'status' => 'pending',
                ]);
                // Re-store the file we just deleted for the reclaimed attempt.
                $file->storeAs('imports', basename($storedPath));

                ProcessImportJob::dispatch($job);

                return response()->json(['id' => $job->id, 'status' => $job->status], 202);
            }

            return response()->json([
                'message' => 'An import for this file is already pending or processing.',
                'existing_job_id' => $conflict?->id,
            ], 409);
        }

        ProcessImportJob::dispatch($job);

        return response()->json([
            'id' => $job->id,
            'status' => $job->status,
        ], 202);
    }

    public function show(int $id): JsonResponse
    {
        $job = ImportJob::findOrFail($id);

        return response()->json([
            'id' => $job->id,
            'filename' => $job->filename,
            'original_filename' => $job->original_filename,
            'status' => $job->status,
            'total_rows' => $job->total_rows,
            'processed_rows' => $job->processed_rows,
            'successful_rows' => $job->successful_rows,
            'failed_rows' => $job->failed_rows,
            'errors_count' => $job->importErrors()->count(),
            'rejected_expires_at' => $job->rejected_expires_at,
            'error_message' => $job->error_message,
            'created_at' => $job->created_at,
        ]);
    }

    public function errors(int $id)
    {
        $job = ImportJob::findOrFail($id);

        if ($job->failed_rows === 0 || $job->rejected_path === null) {
            abort(404);
        }

        if ($job->rejected_expires_at !== null && $job->rejected_expires_at->isPast()) {
            \Storage::disk('local')->delete($job->rejected_path);
            $job->update(['rejected_path' => null]);
            abort(404);
        }

        if (! \Storage::disk('local')->exists($job->rejected_path)) {
            abort(404);
        }

        $filename = 'rejected-' . $job->id . '.csv';

        return \Storage::disk('local')->download($job->rejected_path, $filename, [
            'Content-Type' => 'text/csv',
        ]);
    }
}

<?php

namespace App\Jobs;

use App\Models\ImportJob;
use App\Models\ImportJobError;
use App\Models\User;
use App\Support\CsvImport;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\ShouldQueue;
use Illuminate\Database\QueryException;
use Illuminate\Foundation\Queue\Queueable;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Hash;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Validator;

class ProcessImportJob implements ShouldQueue
{
    use Queueable;

    public int $tries = 1;

    public function __construct(public ImportJob $importJob) {}

    public function handle(): void
    {
        $this->importJob->refresh();

        // No supported same-job rerun: re-dispatch after a terminal state is a no-op.
        if ($this->importJob->isTerminal()) {
            return;
        }

        $storedPath = $this->importJob->stored_path
            ?? ('imports/' . $this->importJob->filename);
        $disk = Storage::disk('local');

        if (! $disk->exists($storedPath)) {
            $this->markFailed('File not found.');
            return;
        }

        $this->importJob->update([
            'status' => 'processing',
            'processing_started_at' => now(),
        ]);

        $fullPath = $disk->path($storedPath);
        $handle = fopen($fullPath, 'r');

        if ($handle === false) {
            $this->markFailed('Unable to open import file.');
            return;
        }

        $header = fgetcsv($handle);

        if ($header === false || ! CsvImport::headerValid($header)) {
            fclose($handle);
            $this->markFailed('Invalid CSV header. Expected: name,email,password.');
            return;
        }

        $flushEvery = max(1, (int) config('imports.chunk_flush', 100));
        $defaultPassword = (string) config('imports.default_password', 'password');

        $total = 0;
        $processed = 0;
        $success = 0;
        $failed = 0;
        $rowNumber = 1; // header is row 1

        try {
            while (($fields = fgetcsv($handle)) !== false) {
                $rowNumber++;
                $total++;

                // Skip wholly-empty lines without penalising counts.
                if ($fields === [null] || (count($fields) === 1 && trim((string) $fields[0]) === '')) {
                    $this->recordError($rowNumber, [], ['row' => ['Empty row.']]);
                    $failed++;
                    $processed++;
                } elseif (count($fields) !== count($header)) {
                    $this->recordError($rowNumber, [], ['row' => ['Column count does not match header.']]);
                    $failed++;
                    $processed++;
                } else {
                    $combined = array_combine($header, $fields);
                    assert($combined !== false);

                    $name = trim((string) ($combined['name'] ?? ''));
                    $email = trim((string) ($combined['email'] ?? ''));
                    $password = $combined['password'] ?? null;
                    $password = is_string($password) ? trim($password) : $password;

                    if ($password === null || $password === '') {
                        $password = $defaultPassword;
                    }

                    $row = ['name' => $name, 'email' => $email, 'password' => $password];

                    $validator = Validator::make($row, [
                        'name' => 'required|string|max:255',
                        'email' => 'required|email|unique:users,email',
                        'password' => 'required|string|min:8',
                    ]);

                    if ($validator->fails()) {
                        $this->recordError($rowNumber, $row, $validator->errors()->toArray());
                        $failed++;
                    } else {
                        try {
                            User::create([
                                'name' => $row['name'],
                                'email' => $row['email'],
                                'password' => Hash::make($row['password']),
                            ]);
                            $success++;
                        } catch (QueryException $e) {
                            if (! self::isEmailDuplicate($e)) {
                                throw $e;
                            }
                            $this->recordError($rowNumber, $row, [
                                'email' => ['This email is already taken.'],
                            ]);
                            $failed++;
                        }
                    }
                    $processed++;
                }

                if ($processed % $flushEvery === 0) {
                    $this->flushProgress($total, $processed, $success, $failed);
                }
            }
        } catch (\Throwable $e) {
            fclose($handle);
            $this->flushProgress($total, $processed, $success, $failed);
            $this->markFailed($e->getMessage());
            return;
        }

        fclose($handle);

        $status = $failed === 0 ? 'completed' : 'completed_with_errors';

        $rejectedPath = null;
        $rejectedExpiresAt = null;

        if ($failed > 0) {
            $rejectedPath = 'imports/rejected/' . $this->importJob->id . '.csv';
            $this->writeRejectedCsv($rejectedPath);
            $rejectedExpiresAt = now()->addDays((int) config('imports.rejected_ttl_days', 7));
        }

        $this->importJob->update([
            'status' => $status,
            'total_rows' => $total,
            'processed_rows' => $processed,
            'successful_rows' => $success,
            'failed_rows' => $failed,
            'rejected_path' => $rejectedPath,
            'rejected_expires_at' => $rejectedExpiresAt,
            'dedupe_key' => null,
        ]);
    }

    public function failed(\Throwable $e): void
    {
        // Safety net only (fatal/timeout where handle()'s catch never ran).
        // Never invents counts: preserves whatever was last flushed.
        $this->importJob->refresh();

        if ($this->importJob->isTerminal()) {
            return;
        }

        $this->importJob->update([
            'status' => 'failed',
            'error_message' => $e->getMessage(),
            'dedupe_key' => null,
        ]);
    }

    private function flushProgress(int $total, int $processed, int $success, int $failed): void
    {
        $this->importJob->update([
            'total_rows' => $total,
            'processed_rows' => $processed,
            'successful_rows' => $success,
            'failed_rows' => $failed,
            'processing_started_at' => now(),
        ]);
    }

    private function markFailed(string $message): void
    {
        $this->importJob->update([
            'status' => 'failed',
            'error_message' => $message,
            'dedupe_key' => null,
        ]);
    }

    /**
     * Store a redacted error row: never persists the password value.
     */
    private function recordError(int $rowNumber, array $row, array $errors): void
    {
        ImportJobError::updateOrCreate(
            ['import_job_id' => $this->importJob->id, 'row_number' => $rowNumber],
            [
                'row_data' => [
                    'name' => $row['name'] ?? null,
                    'email' => $row['email'] ?? null,
                ],
                'errors' => $errors,
            ]
        );
    }

    private function writeRejectedCsv(string $rejectedPath): void
    {
        $errors = ImportJobError::where('import_job_id', $this->importJob->id)
            ->orderBy('row_number')
            ->get();

        $stream = fopen('php://temp', 'r+');
        fputcsv($stream, ['row_number', 'name', 'email', 'errors']);

        foreach ($errors as $error) {
            $rowData = $error->row_data ?? [];
            $flat = collect($error->errors ?? [])
                ->map(fn ($messages, $field) => $field . ': ' . implode(', ', (array) $messages))
                ->values()
                ->implode('; ');
            fputcsv($stream, [
                $error->row_number,
                $rowData['name'] ?? '',
                $rowData['email'] ?? '',
                $flat,
            ]);
        }

        rewind($stream);
        $contents = stream_get_contents($stream);
        fclose($stream);

        Storage::disk('local')->put($rejectedPath, $contents);
    }

    /**
     * True only for a proven UNIQUE violation on users.email — never for other
     * 23000-class errors (NOT NULL, CHECK, other indexes) or outages.
     */
    public static function isEmailDuplicate(QueryException $e): bool
    {
        $errorInfo = $e->errorInfo ?? [];
        $sqlState = $errorInfo[0] ?? null;

        if ($sqlState !== '23000' && $e->getCode() !== '23000' && (int) $e->getCode() !== 23000) {
            // Fall back to message inspection when errorInfo is unavailable.
            if (! str_contains($e->getMessage(), '23000')) {
                return false;
            }
        }

        $driverCode = $errorInfo[1] ?? null;
        $message = $e->getMessage();

        // MySQL: error 1062 naming the email unique index.
        if ($driverCode === 1062 || str_contains($message, 'Duplicate entry')) {
            return str_contains($message, 'users_email_unique')
                || str_contains($message, 'users.email')
                || str_contains($message, "'email'");
        }

        // SQLite: error 19 with the exact table.column in the message.
        if ($driverCode === 19 || str_contains($message, 'UNIQUE constraint failed')) {
            return str_contains($message, 'UNIQUE constraint failed: users.email');
        }

        return false;
    }
}

class PruneRejectedImportFiles extends Command
{
    protected $signature = 'imports:prune-rejected';

    protected $description = 'Delete expired rejected-rows CSVs and reap stale processing import jobs.';

    public function handle(): int
    {
        $disk = Storage::disk('local');

        $expired = ImportJob::whereNotNull('rejected_path')
            ->where('rejected_expires_at', '<', now())
            ->get();

        foreach ($expired as $job) {
            $disk->delete($job->rejected_path);
            $job->update(['rejected_path' => null]);
        }

        $this->reapStale();

        $this->info("Pruned {$expired->count()} rejected file(s).");

        return self::SUCCESS;
    }

    private function reapStale(): void
    {
        $threshold = now()->subMinutes(CsvImport::staleThresholdMinutes());

        ImportJob::where('status', 'processing')
            ->where('processing_started_at', '<', $threshold)
            ->chunkById(100, function ($jobs) {
                foreach ($jobs as $job) {
                    $job->update([
                        'status' => 'failed',
                        'error_message' => 'Stale worker; reaped by imports:prune-rejected.',
                        'dedupe_key' => null,
                    ]);
                }
            });
    }
}

What was built:
- Migration: `import_jobs` gained `original_filename`, `stored_path`, `file_hash`, `dedupe_key` (unique, nullable — active-job lock), `processing_started_at` heartbeat, `successful_rows`/`failed_rows`, `rejected_path`/`rejected_expires_at`; new `import_job_errors` table with `unique(import_job_id, row_number)`.

- `ProcessImportJob`: single-pass streaming, per-row validation (blank password defaulted before validating), redacted error upserts, narrow `isEmailDuplicate()` proof (index-specific, not bare 23000), periodic counter flush + heartbeat, exception-path flush with `failed()` as safety net only, `$tries = 1` with terminal re-dispatch as no-op, rejects CSV (`row_number,name,email,errors` — no passwords) with 7-day TTL.
- `GET /api/imports/{id}` exposes new counters; `GET /api/imports/{id}/errors` downloads the rejects CSV; `imports:prune-rejected` (every 10 min) prunes expired artifacts and reaps stale `processing` jobs.
